literal: He died; posthumous name Prince Mi.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Mi.

literal: His son Jinglüe succeeded and held the post of governor of Binzhou.
idiomatic: His son Jinglüe succeeded and served as governor of Binzhou.

literal: He died; posthumous name Prince Hui.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Hui.

literal: Prince of Anding Xiu, enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing.
idiomatic: Prince of Anding Xiu was enfeoffed in Huangxing 2.

literal: In youth he was clever and keen.
idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and quick.

literal: As Grand Judge of the Outer Capital he was famed for deciding cases.
idiomatic: As Grand Judge of the Outer Capital he won fame for judging cases.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, he headed the Grand Marshal's office.
idiomatic: When the court campaigned south, he headed the Grand Marshal's office.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen personally reviewed the armies; he met Xiu taking three thieves to parade before the six armies and about to behead them, but an edict pardoned them.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen reviewed the armies in person and found Xiu parading three thieves before the six armies to behead them; an edict pardoned the men.

literal: Xiu held fast and said: "If they are not beheaded, how can theft be stilled?"
idiomatic: Xiu held fast and said, "If they are not beheaded, how will theft be stilled?"

literal: The edict said: "The kingly body also has times of extraordinary grace; though this violates military law, they may be specially spared."
idiomatic: The edict answered, "A king may show extraordinary grace; though this breaks military law, spare them."

literal: Xiu then obeyed the edict.
idiomatic: Xiu then obeyed the edict.

literal: The emperor said to the Minister of Education Feng Dan: "The Grand Marshal is stern and holds to the law—the armies must be careful."
idiomatic: The emperor told Minister of Education Feng Dan, "The Grand Marshal is stern in law—the armies must take care."

literal: Thereupon the six armies were all in awe.
idiomatic: Thereupon the six armies stood in awe.

literal: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Xiu followed the carriage to Ye; he was ordered to lead the civil and military who followed the carriage to bring their families from Pingcheng; the emperor personally saw Xiu off north of the Zhang River.
idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, Xiu followed the court to Ye, led the following officials to fetch their families from Pingcheng, and was seen off by the emperor north of the Zhang River.

literal: In the eighteenth year Xiu took to his bed ill; the emperor visited his residence, weeping as he inquired after him; palace envoys with medicine and physicians filled the road one after another.
idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Xiu fell ill; the emperor visited his house in tears, and envoys with physicians crowded the road.

literal: From death until the encoffining the imperial carriage visited three times.
idiomatic: From his death until the encoffining the emperor visited three times.

literal: The emperor came to his gate, changed into coarse hemp, plain cap with mourning headband.
idiomatic: The emperor came to his gate, changed into coarse hemp mourning dress, plain cap with headband.

literal: The crown prince and all officials followed in performing mourning rites.
idiomatic: The crown prince and all officials followed in the mourning rites.

literal: Posthumous name Prince Jing.
idiomatic: His posthumous name was Prince Jing.

literal: An edict posthumously granted the golden axe of authority, added feathered canopy and martial pipes, all matching the rites of the Elder of State Wei Yuan.
idiomatic: An edict granted him posthumously the golden axe, feathered canopy, and martial pipes, all matching Elder of State Wei Yuan.

literal: The emperor personally escorted him beyond the outer wall, weeping as he returned.
idiomatic: The emperor escorted him beyond the wall and returned weeping.

literal: No prince received such favor in rites.
idiomatic: No other prince was honored with such rites.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was given sacrifice in the ancestral temple.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he received sacrifice in the ancestral temple.

literal: His son Chao, courtesy name Huasheng, succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Chao, courtesy Huasheng, succeeded.

literal: At the time Hu Guozhen was enfeoffed Duke of Anding; he was changed to Prince of Beiping, later restored to his original enfeoffment.
idiomatic: At the time Hu Guozhen held Duke of Anding; Chao was shifted to Prince of Beiping, then restored to Anding.

literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he was killed while seeking refuge.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he was killed while seeking refuge.

literal: Jingshan, courtesy name Baoyue, in youth had capacity and vision, and ability surpassing others.
idiomatic: Jingshan, courtesy Baoyue, had capacity and vision in youth and ability beyond most men.

literal: Under Emperor Jing of Zhou he was repeatedly promoted for military merit to Commissioner with the Golden Seal and equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing of Zhou he rose by military merit to Commissioner with the Golden Seal, equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, for merit he was made Grand General, Duke of Pingyuan commandery, and Commander of Bozhou.
idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was made Grand General, Duke of Pingyuan, and Commander of Bozhou.

literal: His laws were clear and stern, bandits vanished from his tracks, and within his jurisdiction all was quiet.
idiomatic: His laws were clear and stern, bandits vanished, and his district grew quiet.

literal: He was summoned to be Director of Attendants.
idiomatic: He was summoned to be Director of Attendants.

literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he followed the Senior Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan in planning for Huainan.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he followed Senior Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan in planning for Huainan.

literal: Commander of Yunzhou Yuwen Liang rebelled and with light troops struck Xiaokuan.
idiomatic: Commander of Yunzhou Yuwen Liang rebelled and struck Xiaokuan with light troops.

literal: Xiaokuan was pressed by Liang; Jingshan struck and broke him.
idiomatic: Xiaokuan was hard pressed; Jingshan struck and broke Liang.

literal: For merit he was made Commander of Bozhou.
idiomatic: For merit he was again made Commander of Bozhou.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Yu Chi Jiong rose in rebellion.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Yu Chi Jiong rose in rebellion.

literal: Governor of Rongzhou Yuwen Zhou conspired with Jiong and secretly sent a letter to urge Jingshan.
idiomatic: Governor of Rongzhou Yuwen Zhou conspired with Jiong and secretly urged Jingshan by letter.

literal: Jingshan seized the envoy, sealed the letter, and sent it to the chief minister's office; he was advanced to Grand General Supreme.
idiomatic: Jingshan seized the envoy, sealed the letter, and sent it to the chief minister's office, and was advanced to Grand General Supreme.

literal: For military merit he was transferred to Commander of Anzhou and advanced to Pillar of State.
idiomatic: For military merit he was made Commander of Anzhou and advanced to Pillar of State.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was made Senior Pillar of State.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the throne, he was made Senior Pillar of State.

literal: The next year, in a great campaign against Chen, Jingshan was made campaign commander-in-chief and marched out of Hankou.
idiomatic: The next year, in the great campaign against Chen, Jingshan was commander-in-chief and marched from Hankou.

literal: About to cross the Yangzi, it happened that Emperor Xuan of Chen died; an edict ordered withdrawal.
idiomatic: About to cross the Yangzi, he learned that Emperor Xuan of Chen had died; an edict ordered withdrawal.

literal: Jingshan's great fame made the enemy deeply fear him.
idiomatic: Jingshan's fame was so great that enemies deeply feared him.

literal: Several years later, for an offense he was dismissed.
idiomatic: Several years later he was dismissed for an offense.

literal: He died at home; posthumously made Commander of Liangzhou, posthumous name Xiang.
idiomatic: He died at home and was posthumously made Commander of Liangzhou, posthumous name Xiang.

literal: His son Chengshou succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Chengshou succeeded.

literal: Chengshou was skilled in bow and horse and served as armory attendant to the Prince of Qin.
idiomatic: Chengshou was skilled with bow and horse and served as armory attendant to the Prince of Qin.

literal: In the Daye era he was Commandant of Xiping commandery.
idiomatic: In the Daye era he was Commandant of Xiping commandery.

literal: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was wild and unrestrained in conduct.
idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was wild and unrestrained.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Supervising Attendant; his depravity grew daily—murder, robbery, public and private all suffered.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Supervising Attendant; his depravity grew daily in murder and robbery until all suffered.

literal: The emperor, because he was close kin, could not bear to bring him under the law;
idiomatic: Because he was close kin, the emperor could not bear to punish him by law;

literal: he was removed from office and confined in a separate lodge.
idiomatic: he was removed from office and confined in a separate lodge.

literal: The lodge was named Hall of Complete Reflection, in hope he would restrain his thoughts.
idiomatic: The lodge was named Hall of Complete Reflection, in hope he would restrain his thoughts.

literal: When the emperor died, he was then able to come out.
idiomatic: When the emperor died, he was allowed out.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because he would not reform, he was returned to the separate lodge and confined as before.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because he would not reform, he was returned to the lodge and confined as before.

literal: After a long while he was released to his home and handed to the Imperial Clan Director for strict admonition and guidance.
idiomatic: After long confinement he was released home and handed to the Imperial Clan Director for strict guidance.

literal: Later he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry on the Direct Path and Forward General.
idiomatic: Later he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry on the Direct Path and Forward General.

literal: For stripping his wife Lady Wang naked before their sons and daughters, and also forcing his wife's younger sister before her mother, Chief Commandant Hou Gang judged it unnatural conduct and sentenced him to strangulation.
idiomatic: For stripping his wife Lady Wang before their children and raping her sister before her mother, Chief Commandant Hou Gang judged unnatural conduct and sentenced him to strangulation.

literal: He met an amnesty and was spared; demoted to Regular Attendant Outside the Sequence.
idiomatic: An amnesty spared him; he was demoted to Regular Attendant Outside the Sequence.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: The appraisal says: Among the sons of Yangping, Yi alone was loyal and stalwart.
idiomatic: The appraisal says: Among the sons of Yangping, Yi alone was loyal and stalwart.

literal: Of the Jingzhao succession, 忄妻 truly had a name.
idiomatic: Of the Jingzhao line, Xun truly had a name.

literal: Kuang's blunt uprightness is well worth praise!
idiomatic: Kuang's blunt uprightness is well worth praise!

literal: When Emperor Xianwen was about to abdicate, it may be called the great integrity of the state.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen was about to abdicate, it was the great test of the state's integrity.

literal: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly at court; his virtuous words shone clear—one word raised the state; is this not what is meant?
idiomatic: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly in court; his virtuous words shone—one sentence raised the state; is this not the thing?

literal: Wenxuan was upright, firm, lofty, and far-seeing, luxuriant as a clan hero, serving many reigns in person.
idiomatic: Wenxuan was upright, firm, lofty, and far-seeing, a luxuriant hero of the clan who served many reigns in person.

literal: Calm in ease and danger alike, he bore the altars of state—is this not the hope of a beam and pillar?
idiomatic: Calm in ease and danger alike, he bore the altars of state—the very hope of beam and pillar.

literal: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the air of Ji An; unused in his time, he met violent death by chance—a pity!
idiomatic: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the air of Ji An; unused in his time, he met violent death by chance—a pity!

literal: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was a man who tore the cap.
idiomatic: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was a man who tore the cap.

literal: Nan'an traced beginning and end; good did not cover evil.
idiomatic: Nan'an traced beginning and end; good did not cover evil.

literal: Ying's use as commander and general made a name in his time.
idiomatic: Ying's use as commander made a name in his time.

literal: The brothers Xi and Lüe early spread men's praise; one was talented but his aim too large, one narrow in capacity yet given wide charge.
idiomatic: The brothers Xi and Lüe won early praise; one had talent but aims too large, one narrow in capacity yet given wide charge.

literal: None could finish their fame and merit; all met untimely death—a pity!
idiomatic: None could finish their fame; all met untimely death—a pity!

literal: Prince Kang was not long-lived; Luan raised the family's name.
idiomatic: Prince Kang was not long-lived; Luan raised the family's name.

literal: Hui adorned his wit and bent his feelings, fawning outside while jealous within—the disaster of Yong'an, who bore the blame?
idiomatic: Hui adorned his wit and bent his feelings, fawning outside while jealous within—the disaster of Yong'an: who bore the blame?

literal: When he died, it was surely fitting!
idiomatic: When he died, it was surely fitting!

literal: Zhangwu and Leling scarcely count.
idiomatic: Zhangwu and Leling scarcely count.

literal: Prince Jing was decisive in judgment, stern in authority, praised in the Taihe era—beautiful!
idiomatic: Prince Jing judged decisively and bore stern authority, praised in the Taihe era—beautiful!
